task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: effect of substitution on shot selection

historical_evidence.finding: With lineup FE the slope was -0.0255; without them -0.0063, and the same-shooter placebo on other play types was -0.0071 to -0.0075, consistent with a shooter-level confound.
The excess was reproduced by a within-unit permutation null (0.3798 vs 0.3744, z 0.40), indicating a mechanical effect under the selection rule; drift-centering removes the tail asymmetry.

Stacked suppression (-0.071, n=1,047) was smaller than either alone and far below the additive prediction (-0.232); one cluster gradient had an unexpected sign and per-player stacked n was often under 5.
Penalty contrast not distinct from placebos; standard errors not printed; evidence of potential placebo dependence.

failed_approaches.why: C_artifact (apparent effect produced by construction, selection or labeling flaw) with risk of confounding and placebo dependence.
[prior work], [prior work], [prior work]; RISK:DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY, RISK:EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, RISK:MECHANICAL_FLOOR, RISK:PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE.

evidence_establishes: Lineup fixed effects can substantially reduce apparent effects that are actually due to shooter-level confounding.
Selection of high-impact units can create mechanical artifacts that mimic real effects.
Small sample sizes and implementation bugs can bias results.
Placebo contrasts are essential to detect whether an effect is genuine.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix in a measurable way.
The magnitude or direction of personnel effects on shot mix with the available data.
The feasibility of isolating lineup effects from game context in this dataset.
own_inferences: The question is conceptually testable but requires a design that explicitly controls for lineup and player fixed effects, uses same-player placebos, and accounts for game-state variables. The data contain enough detail (substitution intervals, shot data, defensive matchup minutes) to model these effects, though sample sizes per specific lineup combination may be limited. A high-dimensional fixed-effects regression or hierarchical model with careful variable selection and pre-registered hypotheses can mitigate known risks.
uncertainties: Exact distribution of lineup combinations across seasons; whether each lineup has sufficient possessions to estimate shot mix changes; potential measurement error in shot distance or type; unobserved confounders such as coaching strategy changes.

historical_effect.explanation: No retrieved record directly addresses personnel effects on shot mix; the existing records illustrate general pitfalls that must be avoided but do not resolve the question.

blocking_constraints.text: Lineup changes are correlated with player quality and game context, risking omitted-variable bias.
Some lineup combinations occur rarely, limiting statistical power.
Season-to-season changes in play style or rule changes may make effect sizes nonstationary.
Differentiating genuine lineup effects from shooter-level adaptation requires robust placebo tests.
Testing multiple shot mix metrics increases false-positive risk.

prior_work.summary: No prior study with the same data and question has been found in the retrieval; existing studies highlight methodological concerns rather than provide evidence.

risks.text: Lineup changes may be driven by game context and player performance, confounding the estimated effect.
Rare lineup configurations reduce estimation precision.
Temporal changes in offensive strategies could bias effect estimates.
Without proper placebo checks, observed changes might be artifacts.
Simultaneous testing of several shot mix outcomes inflates type I error.

design.estimand: Difference in average shot mix (e.g., average shot distance, shot type proportions) attributable to a change in the offensive five, holding lineup, player, and game-state fixed.
design.unit: Individual possessions (or possession-level aggregates) within the 2022‑23, 2023‑24, and 2024‑25 seasons.
design.sample: All possessions with complete substitution, shot, and defensive matchup data; only those with at least 20 minutes of play for the specific lineup to ensure stability.
design.power: Target 80% power to detect a 0.1‑standard‑deviation shift in average shot distance, using cross‑season pooled data and a hierarchical linear model; conduct a priori power analysis using estimated intraclass correlation from pilot data.
design.controls: Lineup fixed effects (for both offense and defense), player fixed effects, game‑state controls (score differential, period, quarter, time remaining), and opponent strength variables.
design.falsification: Same‑player placebo test: compare shot mix changes for a player when they play the same position in different lineups; also test a negative control where lineup changes occur but no actual personnel change (e.g., same player swapped with identical replacement).
design.multiplicity: Pre‑register a single primary outcome (average shot distance). Apply Holm-Bonferroni correction for any secondary outcomes (shot type proportions, effective field goal percentage).
design.decision_rule: Reject the null of no lineup effect if the 95% CI for the estimated effect excludes zero after adjustment; otherwise fail to reject.
design.data_version: 2026‑11‑02 dataset, encompassing NBA 2022‑23, 2023‑24, and 2024‑25 regular season and playoffs per-game files, play‑by‑play, substitution intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes, and derived possession records.
